$ FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test  # ladder-a
    The root-package check for the module-root corpus runs in normal runs, so it runs after the update: go test ./...
    what ran, in order:
        parse ran on x
        resolve ran on x
        evaluate's probe ran
        evaluate ran on x
--- PASS: TestCorpus
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/script
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/evaluate
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/parse
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/resolve
PASS
$ edit c/corpus_test.go  # a package c over the corpus
$ FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./b  # ladder-b-suite
--- PASS: TestCorpus
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/script
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/parse
PASS
$ FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./c  # ladder-b-owns
    script/x: The root package, ., owns parse, resolve and evaluate, and ./b uses parse for outline.
        parse: Parses the script, as its parse/ tree says.
        out/parse/values.txt is an output the run no longer produces.
        If the run should still write it, fix the code. If not, delete the section by hand; FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./... leaves it in place.
    what ran, in order:
        parse ran on x
        outline's probe ran
        outline ran on x
--- FAIL: TestCorpus
    --- FAIL: TestCorpus/script
        --- FAIL: TestCorpus/script/x
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/outline
            --- FAIL: TestCorpus/script/x/parse
FAIL
[exit 1]
$ go test  # ladder-a
    the column parse is owned by ./b as a suite, and by . and ./c, each as a lift. Lifts share the suites' column names, which are unique per corpus root, and one package owns each column.
        Rename the suite or the lift. Of . and ./c, which own the lift, a package that only reads its product gives it to hypercase.Use in place of hypercase.Own.
    script/x: The root package, ., owns parse, resolve and evaluate, and ./b uses parse for outline.
        parse: Parses the script, as its parse/ tree says.
        out/parse/values.txt is an output the run no longer produces.
        If the run should still write it, fix the code. If not, delete the section by hand; FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./... leaves it in place.
    what ran, in order:
        parse ran on x
        resolve ran on x
        evaluate's probe ran
        evaluate ran on x

FAIL
[exit 1]

$ go test  # ladder-a-useonly
    the column parse is owned by ./b and ./c, each as a suite. Column names are unique per corpus root, and one package owns each column.
        Rename one of the suites, or remove one.
    the column parse is owned by ./b and ./c, each as a suite, and used by . as a lift. Lifts share the suites' column names, which are unique per corpus root.
        Rename the suite or the lift.
    the lift parse is used by ., and no package owns it, so its error is recorded nowhere.
        Once the suite and the lift have different names, own the lift in one of them: give it to hypercase.Own in place of hypercase.Use.
    testdata/script/x.txtar: no registry claims out/outline/outcome and out/outline/values.txt: no column named outline runs over the corpus script.
        If a column should write them, register the column. If not, delete them by hand; FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./... leaves them in place.
    what ran, in order:
        parse ran on x
        resolve ran on x
        evaluate's probe ran
        evaluate ran on x
--- FAIL: TestCorpus
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/script
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/evaluate
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/resolve
FAIL
[exit 1]
